name: α-Terpineol

pubchem.title: Alpha-Terpineol
pubchem.description: Alpha-terpineol is a terpineol that is propan-2-ol substituted by a 4-methylcyclohex-3-en-1-yl group at position 2. It has a role as a plant metabolite.

consumer_summary.what_it_is: Alpha-terpineol is a naturally occurring terpene alcohol that plays a key role in the scent profiles of many essential oils. It is widely known for its pleasant, lilac-like floral aroma, making it a popular ingredient in perfumes, cosmetics, and flavorings. In daily life, you are most likely to encounter it when smelling fresh herbs, citrus fruits, or botanical personal care products.
consumer_summary.found_in: This fragrant molecule is abundant in tea tree oil (Melaleuca alternifolia) and is also found in familiar kitchen staples like lemon, bay laurel, rosemary, and ginger.
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Researchers are drawn to alpha-terpineol because of its prominent role in traditional botanical extracts like tea tree oil, prompting investigations into its biological activity. Scientists are particularly interested in its potential to interact with cellular pathways, exploring its effects on microbial growth, oxidative stress, and cellular health. The strongest evidence so far comes from human observational studies (Oxford level 2b), which are helping to map how this fragrant compound might influence human biology.

structure_function.statement: Early observational work points toward alpha-terpineol's potential to support the body's natural defenses against microbial challenges.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Researchers are exploring whether alpha-terpineol can influence tumor cell behavior, with early studies investigating its ability to suppress aggressive cellular traits. If this bears out, it could become a valuable naturally derived compound in supportive oncology research.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial in patients with specific solid tumors, measuring tumor markers and progression-free survival over 12 months alongside standard care.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Scientists are investigating whether alpha-terpineol's prominent presence in antimicrobial botanicals like tea tree oil translates to direct, clinically useful antibacterial or antifungal properties. If confirmed, it could offer a new avenue for topical or systemic microbial defense.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized controlled trial applying a standardized topical alpha-terpineol formulation versus a placebo in adults with mild to moderate superficial skin infections, measuring microbial clearance rates over 14 days.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Early animal work points toward alpha-terpineol having a soothing effect on pain pathways, prompting researchers to ask if it could serve as a non-habit-forming analgesic. If this holds up, it could provide a novel botanical option for managing everyday aches.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A phase 1/2 human clinical trial administering oral alpha-terpineol to healthy volunteers subjected to a standardized pain stimulus (like the cold pressor test), measuring subjective pain scores and tolerance time over a 4-hour period.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Researchers are exploring whether alpha-terpineol can protect neural tissues from stress and damage. If this bears out, it could open doors for its use in supporting long-term cognitive and neurological health.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized, placebo-controlled human trial in older adults with mild cognitive impairment, administering a daily alpha-terpineol supplement and measuring cognitive function scores and inflammatory biomarkers over 6 months.

associated_conditions.relationship: Noted as an occupational exposure hazard in industrial settings.

consumer_summary.cautions: In industrial settings where it is used as a concentrated solvent, acute exposure to alpha-terpineol is recognized as an occupational hazard.
consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: Best evidence so far is human observational work (Oxford 2b); most of the rest is animal and lab research.
